blocks.text: Daniel checked the cuffs once more. Jenny pulled against them when he reached her chair, but none opened.
“You’ve made your point,” she said. “Let me go.”
“Not until your friends arrive.” He turned toward Luke. “Zerdo will come for her. Keep an eye out.”
Luke glanced at the empty station beside Jenny. Then he rose toward the small basement window high above the workbench, facing the sunken yard.
“Just watch,” Daniel said. “If you see the boy, let him come in.”
“And the glove?”
Daniel looked up. “Keep it out.”
blocks.alt: Daniel sends Luke toward the high laboratory window to watch for Zerdo. Jenny remains secured by all four cuffs in civilian clothes; the second station is empty.

blocks.text: Luke slipped through the window and rose out of the yard toward the roofs. Jenny watched his shadow pass over the glass. Daniel lowered the window and latched it, then went to the service door and opened it wide.
At Billy’s office, the appointed hour passed without a call.
He found the laboratory number in his directory. Daniel answered as though he had been beside the telephone waiting for it.
“Put Jenny on,” Billy said.
“She’s still occupied with the demonstration.”
“Then interrupt it.”
“I’m sure she’ll tell you all about it when we’re finished.”
The line went dead. Billy held the receiver a moment, then dialed Seth’s home number.
“She hasn’t called. Daniel won’t let me speak to her.”
“I’m coming.”
“Put your suit on. Meet me by the steps to the laboratory’s service yard. We check what’s happening before anyone goes in.”
Fist hovered beside the open office window. He had heard enough.
“I’ll look from above.”
“Stay clear of the windows,” Billy said. “Come back and tell us what you see.”

The glove shot out over the street. Billy reached for the telephone again to report Jenny missing and give the police the address and the directions downstairs. Then he put down the receiver, locked his office and hurried out to meet Seth.
Fist reached the roofs above the laboratory building first. Below him, steps dropped from the alley into the sunken yard. The service door stood open. No one waited on the steps.
He slowed beside a chimney, staying back from the roof’s edge as he looked down toward the yard.
Iron teeth struck his cuff from behind.
Fist twisted free, leaving a ragged strip of white fabric between the teeth. Luke swept past him, turned, and came straight back.
“You again,” Fist said. “Should’ve guessed.”
He drove forward to meet him. His damaged cuff caught against a railing as he turned, pulling him sideways. Luke’s iron jaw slammed into his red leather and sent him scraping along the steel bars.
Fist rose crookedly. A dark scuff ran across his knuckles.
blocks.alt: Above the Cleveland rooftops, Luke’s iron jaws drive a surprised Fist toward a steel railing. Fist’s red leather is visibly scuffed and his empty white cuff is torn.

blocks.text: Luke gave him no room to recover. He chased the glove beneath a rooftop sign, forcing him toward its iron supports. Fist ducked the first beam. The second caught his side with a sharp scrape.
“You had to wait until I wasn’t looking?” Fist snapped.
Luke struck again. Fist tried to turn the blow into a punch, but the iron teeth closed on the edge of his padding. He pulled loose with a painful wrench and dropped toward the roof.
Luke hovered above him, blocking the open sky.
“No one will stop me from getting my body back.”
“Your uncle did this to you.” Fist struggled to rise. “Not us.”
“He’s going to fix it.”
Luke drove him against the base of the sign. Fist’s leather folded against the iron. He tried to push away, but Luke caught his torn cuff and held him there.
For a moment, the glove’s eyes squeezed shut. His next shove barely moved the jaw.
blocks.alt: A close view shows Fist struggling low above a rooftop with scuffed, creased red leather and a torn white cuff while Luke’s iron jaws loom above him.

blocks.text: On the street below, Seth came around the corner in his blue suit. He looked for Billy, then up toward the roofs. He could not see Fist behind the sign.
At the end of the alley, stone steps led down into the sunken service yard. The basement door was open.
blocks.alt: Seth reaches the open laboratory entrance and sees Jenny still locked into her restraint station beyond the benches. Jenny calls a warning toward him.

blocks.text: Seth hurried down the steps. From the open threshold, he could see through the front room and the workshop doorway. Beyond the bench, Jenny sat against the metal backing of her chair.
“Jenny?”
She heard him. Her chair faced far enough toward the workshop doorway that she could see his red mask beyond the bench, at the service entrance.
“Seth, stay—”
He saw the steel around her wrists and started toward her. She pulled hard against the cuffs, trying to make him look at her instead of them.
“It’s a trap!”
The service door slammed behind him. Gas hissed from the vents.
Seth had already drawn breath to answer her. He covered his mouth and reached Jenny’s chair, gripping the edge of one cuff.
blocks.alt: Gas curls from the laboratory vents as Seth reaches Jenny’s still-locked wrist cuff. Jenny remains restrained in civilian clothes and tries to warn him; Daniel watches from behind glass.

blocks.text: “Get out!” she shouted.
Jenny turned her face into her shoulder. Her cuffs kept her hands from reaching her mouth. She coughed and tried to draw a smaller breath, but the gas was already making her head heavy.

He planted his thumb against the cuff’s edge and tried to keep his attention there. Jenny coughed beside him, and he looked up. He pulled again, too quickly. The mounting creaked, but his hands slipped before he could bend the cuff clear. His knees hit the floor beside her.
Behind the glass, Daniel watched the boy struggle to lift his head.
Seth reached for Jenny’s hand. He felt her fingers close weakly around his glove, then loosen. Her head sagged against the metal backing. He tried to say her name. Then the room went dark.
Luke waited outside the closed basement window with Fist’s cuff clenched between his teeth. The glove hung below him, scuffed and bent, his eyes open but unfocused.
Daniel switched off the gas and turned on the ventilation. He waited behind the glass until the haze cleared, then stepped out to open the high window for Luke and prepare the second station.
“Put it on the bench,” he told Luke.
Fist tried to lift himself as Luke let go. He managed only a small, uneven rise. Daniel brought down a heavy bird cage from a shelf and pushed him through its open side door.
“Hold still,” he said.
“Make me.”
Fist struck the closing door. The blow shook the cage, but pain ran through his creased leather and he sank onto its metal floor. Daniel slid the latch home and secured it with a padlock.

Jenny woke while Daniel was checking Seth’s ankle cuffs. She blinked until the second chair stopped blurring. Seth’s eyes stayed shut. She tried her own wrists, then her ankles; all four of her original cuffs were still closed.
When Seth woke, his first thought was Jenny’s hand. He tried to reach for it again.
Steel stopped him.
She sat beside him, still in her blouse and pink skirt. He was held against the second station by broad cuffs around his red gloves and boots.
“I tried to tell you,” she said quietly.
“I saw what he’d done to you.” Seth pulled at the armrests. His head swam. He could bend steel when he kept his attention on it, but he could not hold one thought still through the dizziness.
“I know.”
A scrape came from the bench. Fist pressed his scuffed knuckles against the cage bars. His white cuff was torn. He looked at them, then at Luke.
blocks.alt: Seth in his blue and red uniform and Jenny in her white blouse and pink skirt are restrained at adjacent metal stations. Injured Fist is locked in a reinforced bird cage on the bench while Daniel and Luke watch.

blocks.text: “Don’t look so pleased,” he said.
Luke drifted nearer the second station. Seth watched the iron jaws hover above his chest. Daniel put a hand on the back of the chair, smiling.
“There,” he said to his nephew. “I told you I could get him here.”
Seth tried the cuffs once more. Jenny’s stayed shut beside him. Across the bench, Fist’s battered red leather showed between the bars of the locked bird cage.
